title: Fraternity and gym dance bands: McCollum, Armstrong, riverboat bands
summary: Gym dances cost a dollar a couple. For fraternity dances they hired McCollum's cheap band and sometimes Armstrong's loud band. The dance bands he lists include the Silver Leaf and Tuxedo.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I lost track. The minute I started getting a little bit older, the intense interest, when the minute I started going to Tulane, I began to have to study a little bit, and then the music began falling in the background, although we did play once in a while. Now then we began getting our music, as I say through the regular bands. And Oliver, comparatively late, because he began playing up at the gym. I remember I was going up to those gym dances on Saturday night before I was even in Tulane. A dollar a couple. Oh yes, a subscription dance. And all you got was ice water in the band and a hell of a good floor and you'd dance all evening. But before that Oliver period, we used to have fraternity dances. OBD was a high school fraternity. DTO was another one. And they always had dancers and bands. And I remember the bands that they hired at the time, one of them was McCollum's. Whenever they were hired McCollum's band, it was because they couldn't afford a good band. He charged less than the others. And boy, he blew more bad notes than you ever imagined. And he had a bad embouchure because I remember he had a big white button sticking out on his lip that was just like a headlight on him. He always had pretty good men. And one of the men that played with him before the formation of Pierron's band was Louis Warnicke. I have a picture of Louis with McCollum's. I think you gave me a copy of that.

But anyway, another band that they only used when they had to was Louis Armstrong's band. He played, you know, he wasn't the leader. But he blew so damn loud that you had to have a hall as big as the auditorium to take him. And I'm not so sure he was always on the button with his notes either. He only became good, really good, when he began playing on the Steamer. He was the president. No, what is it? The Sidney or Capitola. Yeah, yeah, yeah. The bands that we danced by, the Silverleaf, Mapleleaf, Goldleaf, Tuxedo, as I said, McCollum's. And then a great deal, as we grew a little bit older into the town when we began going out with the debutants, then we began going to Antoine's, you know, it's La Louisiane, which is now, was occupied, the area which is presently occupied by the Playbar Club and Moran's Restaurant. Now, that whole thing was La Louisiane, and their band, the house band there, was Robichaud.
